issue.title: http request param escaping insufficient

body:
We dealt with this same problem in Angular 1 $http with a custom `encodeUriQuery`: https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/53ab8bcde1ee8fa88d06dd3b5ed4986cb141c129/src/Angular.js#L1394

As far as I remember, the `encodeUriQuery` function from ng1 pretty closely matches the ietf spec, so we should just copy it over and use it for Angular 2 http instead of `encodeURIComponent`.

Actually, `encodeUriQuery` doesn't quite get what we need here, since it will still escape slashes.
`q=repo:janbaer%2Fhowcani%2Btype:issue&sort=created&order=desc&page=1 //encodeUriQuery`
`q=repo:janbaer/howcani+type:issue&sort=created&order=desc&page=1 // Before Change`
`q=repo%3Ajanbaer%2Fhowcani%2Btype%3Aissue&sort=created&order=desc&page=1 // Current`

If we added `/` and `+` (`%2F` and `%2B`) to whitelist, which I think are both ok with the spec to be part of query values (but I need to read again), then it would solve this use case. Though since different APIs have different arg requirements, it would be nice to provide the ability to override the serialization mechanism as they did in ng1. https://github.com/angular/angular.js/blob/53ab8bcde1ee8fa88d06dd3b5ed4986cb141c129/src/ng/http.js#L26

I'll look into this more tomorrow.

I'm facing the same issue. Is there any workaround in the meantime ?

Edit: I just subclassed URLSearchParams and overrided the `toString` method for now.

My workaround was to concatenate to searchparams in my own function and use the request options without searchparams.

https://github.com/howcani-project/howcani/commit/8a2fa80b079c9d340952bac371acd1c265b4e10e

issue.title: fix(http): don't encode values that are allowed in query
issue.body:
@vicb still some work to do on this PR, but I hope you can give an initial review and give your thoughts on the approach.

TODO: 
- [ ] Actually inject the QueryEncoder so it can be changed with DI
- [ ] Make the encode a RequestOption property so it can be passed in at runtime (to support multiple encoders for different backends)
- [ ] Add decoding as well, to symmetrically parse query params.
- [ ] Add docs showing how to override encoder

This implements a new class, QueryEncoder, that provides
methods for encoding keys and values of query parameter.
The encoder encodes with encodeURIComponent, and then
decodes a whitelist of allowed characters back to their
unencoded form. QueryEncoder is intended to be provided
to http via Dependency Injection so the default encoding
mechanism can be overridden.

BREAKING CHANGE:

The changes to Http's URLSearchParams serialization now 
prevent encoding of these characters inside query parameters
which were previously converted to percent-encoded values:

@ : $ , ; + ; ? /

Fixes #9348

issue.body:
Back ends for several languages (including Python, PHP and Node.js) expect to receive encoded parameters with some standard conventions, when they receive them as raw decoded strings they can't parse those parameters. This removes the custom decoding of parameters to raw strings and leaves the default standard encoding for HttpClient.

## What is the current behavior?
<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

Currently, when creating URL parameters, some characters are decoded and converted to raw strings after the `encodeURIComponent()` had encoded them. The characters are: `@`, `:`, `$`, `,`, `;`, `+`, `=`, `?`, `/`.

This creates communication problems with back ends in at least Python, PHP and Node.js.

Check the referenced issues for more details on all the possible problems this creates.

Issue Number: #11058 #18884 #18274 #14531 #13077 #18261


## What is the new behavior?

With this PR, when using `URLSearchParams`, the parameters will be encoded as normally, without being decoded by Angular before sending them in the URL to the server.

I created a parallel PR that solves the problem for cases using `HttpParams` here: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/19710.
